text: Woodcourt is his disinterested friend,” I answered. “But I mean in professional attendance, medical attendance.” “That can do little for an unhappy mind,” said I. “Just so,” said Mr. Vholes. So slow, so eager, so bloodless and gaunt, I felt as if Richard were wasting away beneath the eyes of this adviser and there were something of the vampire in him. “Miss Summerson,” said Mr. Vholes, very slowly rubbing his gloved hands, as if, to his cold sense of touch, they were much the same in black kid or out of it, “this was an ill-advised marriage of Mr. C.’s.” I begged he would excuse me from discussing it.
